newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 13.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:
** India's Hindu nationalists said on Sunday they were gearing up to strengthen the party organisation ahead of a general election they expect later this year.
"We have alerted all the party units to be prepared for polls in 1997," Lal Krishan Advani, president of the rightwing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), told reporters.

** The head of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Saturday asked Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram for tax breaks to revive shaky bourses. "It is now agreed by all concerned that our country's capital markets are in a bad shape," BSE president M.G. Damani told Chidambaram in a pre-budget memorandum.

"Individual and institutional investors have suffered heavy losses by way of capital erosion in the last eight months. Investors shall not return to the market unless the following measures are implemented immediately," Damani said.
** In a move to give a fillip to the Indian shipbuilding industry, the Finance Ministry cleared a proposal to provide 30 percent subsidy to the ship builders, the Economic Times says
The subsidy would be provided to the shipyards over and above the cost of building a ship, the paper reports.
The government is expected to present the fiscal budget for 1997/98 (April-March) in the last week of February.
